t.1.156.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard this, the sons of Kuntī became as if pierced by a dart, and all those great chariot-warriors became troubled in mind.
t.1.156.2: Then Kuntī, the speaker of truth, seeing her sons bewildered and dispirited, spoke these words to Yudhiṣṭhira.
t.1.156.3: For many nights we have dwelt here in the brahmin's house, Yudhiṣṭhira, enjoying ourselves in this delightful city and obtaining our alms.
t.1.156.4: All the lovely forests and groves that are here have been seen by us again and again, O tamer of foes.
t.1.156.5: Those same sights, seen again, no longer delight us as they once did; nor, O hero, joy of the Kurus, are alms obtained as they were before.
t.1.156.7: The Pāñcālas, it is said, have plenty of food, O tormentor of foes; and that king Yajñasena, we have heard, is devoted to the brahmins.
t.1.156.6: So let us go to the Pāñcālas, if you think it right. Seeing what we have never seen before will be delightful, dear son.
t.1.156.8: For a long stay in one place is not fitting, nor is it approved by me. So let us go there, if you, my son, think it good.
t.1.156.9: Whatever you consider ought to be done, that is our highest good. But as for my younger brothers, I do not know whether they would go or not.
t.1.156.10: Then Kuntī spoke of departure to Bhīmasena, to Arjuna, and likewise to the twins, and they then said, "So be it."
t.1.156.11: Then, O king, having taken leave of that brahmin, Kuntī set out with her sons for the delightful city of the great-souled Drupada.
